inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2026 (12m to 31-May-2026) consolidated revenue 94,720 less an estimated ~8,900 for FedEx Freight (spun off 1-Jun-2026 as FDXF). The FY2026 10-K consolidates Freight for the full year (no discontinued-operations presentation in the XBRL), so every continuing-business FY0 anchor below is a pro forma estimate, not a filed figure. Freight FY2026 estimate: revenue ~8,900, operating income ~1,500, D&A ~500 (EBITDA ~2,000), capex ~700, FCF ~1,000. Replace with the segment note / Form 10 recast when the transition-period 10-K (Jun-Dec 2026) is filed.
inputs.share_count_basis: FY2026 10-K weighted-average diluted shares 239m (basic 237m); Q3 FY2026 diluted also 239m. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; buybacks (796 in FY2026, 3,017 in FY2025) fund the flat count.
inputs.net_debt_note: As filed at 31-May-2026 (pre-spin, consolidated): LT debt incl. current 23,455 + finance leases 1,514 + other = 25,131; cash 13,311. Operating lease liabilities (17,229) are EXCLUDED because operating lease cost (3,518) sits inside EBITDA (treatment A). The Freight spin-off effects are carried in equity_bridge, not netted here, so the filed numbers stay auditable. Post-spin pro forma net debt is ~8,200 (11,820 less the 4,100 special dividend received from Freight, plus ~500 cash seeded to FDXF; Freight's own pre-spin borrowings and their proceeds leave together, net zero).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Pro forma continuing: FY2026 consolidated FCF 5,116 (OCF 8,925 - capex 3,809) less ~1,000 estimated Freight FCF. Consolidated owner FCF = 5,116 - 177 = 4,939.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income 437 on a 13.3bn pre-spin cash pile, but FedEx is a net-debt company (pro forma ~8.2bn net debt, > 2x FCF base) so interest income is not stripped; the component build is unlevered (EBITDA -> NOPAT) and never carries it anyway.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement ShareBasedCompensation add-back 177 (XBRL, filed 2026-07-20); no separate equity-award tax withholding line is tagged, so the add-back is used as the combined figure. Ex-Freight estimate 160 (~0.19% of revenue).
inputs.fiscal_year_end: 31 May (to FY2026); changed to 31 December from 1-Jun-2026 via a 7-month transition period Jun-Dec 2026
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Rf ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.2 -> cost of equity ~10.2%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.0% (5.2% pre-tax x 0.76). Market cap ~68bn vs gross debt ~25bn (incl. finance leases, excl. operating leases) -> ~26% debt weight -> WACC ~8.6%, used 8.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios (risk charged once via probability weights).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A: operating leases stay in the flows. US-GAAP operating lease cost (3,518 in FY2026) is inside operating expenses, so the EBITDA margin path is post-lease and operating lease liabilities (17,229) are NOT added to net debt. Finance leases (1,514) are in total_debt and their charges are outside EBITDA - consistent.
inputs.nci_treatment: None material; no NCI line in the filings.

First valuation of this ticker. CONTINUITY WARNINGS: (1) The 1-Jun-2026 FedEx Freight spin-off removed ~9% of revenue and ~20% of EBITDA; the FY2026 10-K is fully consolidated, so FY0 is an ex-Freight pro forma built from segment estimates and every historical CAGR describes the consolidated company. (2) The fiscal year moved from May to December; Y1 here is the 12 months from 1-Jun-2026 (7-month transition period + H1 CY2027), which is why 'CY2026' guidance is only a cross-check. (3) The Metrics CSV mislabels the four most recent quarters: rows 'Q3 2025', 'H2-2025', 'Q4 2025' and 'Q1 2026' are actually Q1 FY2026 (Aug-25), H1 FY2026, Q2 FY2026 (Nov-25) and Q3 FY2026 (Feb-26) per the XBRL period dates (the known XBRL fy/fp mislabel); the FY2026 row is correct. No 10-Q for the quarter to 31-Aug-2026 was in the XBRL API at build time, so the filed 31-May-2026 balance sheet is the anchor and the spin is bridged pro forma. Refresh net debt, share count and the FDXF stake from the Aug-2026 10-Q when it lands. Analysis JSON's guidance items (CY2026 adj. EPS ~19.70 midpoint, ~11% revenue growth, ~2bn Network 2.0 savings by end-2027, ~600m stranded overhead) were used as cross-checks: 19.70 x 239m = ~4.7bn adjusted NI implies ~7%+ adjusted EBIT margin vs the ~4.6% GAAP ex-Freight FY0 base; the gap is business-optimization charges, stranded costs and the savings ramp, which the base margin path only half-credits.

equity_bridge.item: 19.9% retained stake in FedEx Freight (FDXF) at market
equity_bridge.note: ~29.4m FDXF shares (237m FDX basic / 2 distributed = 80.1%; 19.9% retained) x $113.18 FDXF close 2026-09-25. To be disposed within 24 months, likely tax-free via debt-for-equity exchange; no haircut applied, but a 20-30% FDXF drawdown is worth ~$3-4/FDX share.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blend: revenue_5yr 2.4% and equity_5yr 5.5%, lifted for FY2026 momentum (+7.7% consolidated, ~+9% ex-Freight) and management's ~11% CY2026 revenue-growth guidance; the base path starts at 6% and decays to 2.5%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 5.5% is >30% above revenue 5yr CAGR 2.4% (retained earnings on a low-growth top line, partly offset by buybacks); EPS 5yr CAGR is negative because FY2021 was the pandemic-surge peak (EPS 19.79). FCF 3yr CAGR of 25.6% is off the FY2023 capex-peak trough and is not a trend. All CAGRs are on the CONSOLIDATED series including FedEx Freight (spun off 1-Jun-2026).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF (reported FCF less SBC) CAGRs are within 0.3pp of reported-FCF CAGRs: SBC is ~0.2% of revenue and not growing faster than cash flow.

base.narrative: FY0 ex-Freight GAAP EBITDA margin ~9.1% (post operating leases, including ~0.7bn business-optimization charges and ~0.6bn stranded overhead). Margin path credits roughly half of the guided ~2bn Network 2.0 savings plus stranded-cost elimination, reaching 11% by Y6 - DRIVE's 4bn was largely absorbed by wage/purchased-transport inflation (FY23 10.1% -> FY25 10.8% consolidated). Capex rises from FY2026's unusually low 3.6% of revenue toward D&A (~4.5%) as the aircraft fleet cycle resumes. Cash tax 24% (FY2026 book rate 23.5%; cash taxes paid 1,912 exceeded expense). Working capital consumes ~3% of incremental revenue (receivables > payables). Terminal cap 15x reflects a cyclical, capital-intensive carrier.

bull.narrative: Management's CY2026 guidance (~11% revenue growth, adj. EPS ~19.70 midpoint) is delivered and the full 2bn Network 2.0 savings plus stranded-cost removal stick, taking EBITDA margin to 12.5% (UPS-like) with B2B/AI-infrastructure and healthcare volumes and surcharge-led yield outrunning wage inflation.

bear.narrative: Amazon Shipping's third-party opening and UPS/USPS price competition take SMB/e-commerce share; a trade-policy/de-minimis-driven international slump and a consumer slowdown hit volumes into a high fixed-cost network; Network 2.0 savings are competed away and stranded costs linger, so the ex-Freight margin never recovers above FY2024-25 levels.

scenario_narratives.base: Pure-play parcel/express FedEx grows revenue 6% in the first post-spin year on rate increases, peak surcharges and B2B strength, fading to 2.5% nominal by year 8 (industry-mature parcel growth). GAAP EBITDA margin expands from ~9.1% ex-Freight to 11% by Y6 as roughly half of the guided Network 2.0 savings and the ~600m stranded-overhead removal reach the bottom line while the rest is absorbed by wage, purchased-transport and fuel inflation, as with DRIVE. Capex normalises to ~4.5% of revenue (~D&A). The 4.1bn Freight dividend and the 19.9% FDXF stake are bridged to equity at cost/market.
scenario_narratives.bull: Network 2.0 delivers its full 2bn and the stranded overhead is gone by end-2027; CY2026 guidance (~11% revenue growth, adj. EPS ~19.70) proves a floor, AI-infrastructure/data-centre freight and healthcare logistics compound, international export lanes recover as tariff policy settles, and the margin reaches 12.5% - the level UPS earned pre-2023. Terminal growth 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Amazon Shipping and price competition erode the SMB e-commerce book while a tariff-driven trade contraction and a weaker US consumer shrink international express and domestic volumes; operating leverage cuts the wrong way, Network 2.0 savings are given back in pricing, and revenue stalls for three years before resuming 2% growth at a 9% EBITDA margin. Elevated post-spin leverage (~8bn net debt plus 17bn of operating leases) limits buybacks but does not threaten solvency.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25%: Amazon opening its logistics network to third parties is a live structural threat to the core e-commerce book, trade/de-minimis policy is unresolved, and the business carries high fixed-cost operating leverage plus more concentration after losing Freight's counter-cyclical LTL earnings. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things (full savings retention, 11% growth, tariff normalisation) and DRIVE's 4bn of savings did not visibly lift consolidated margins. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the post-spin parcel/express carrier on unlevered owner FCF built from a GAAP, post-operating-lease EBITDA margin that expands only as fast as the transformation programme has historically converted savings into margin; capitalise at 15x FCF or Gordon, whichever is lower; bridge the Freight dividend and the retained FDXF stake explicitly rather than guessing a post-spin balance sheet. The valuation depends far more on the terminal EBITDA margin (each 1pp is worth ~$35-40/share) than on growth.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY0 is a pro forma ex-Freight estimate (Freight FY2026 revenue ~8.9bn / EBITDA ~2.0bn assumed); the transition-period 10-K recast could move the base margin by +/-0.5pp
Terminal EBITDA margin: 11% base vs 9.1% FY0 assumes half the guided Network 2.0 savings are retained; DRIVE precedent suggests retention can be lower
Amazon Shipping opening to third parties: volume and yield pressure on the SMB/e-commerce book is the bear axis and is not yet visible in reported numbers
Trade policy: de-minimis elimination and tariffs cost ~1bn in FY2026; a further contraction in Asia-US lanes hits the highest-yield international express volumes
Balance sheet: post-spin net debt ~8.2bn plus 17.2bn operating leases and a capex cycle turning up (aircraft); 31-May-2026 anchors predate the spin and must be refreshed from the Aug-2026 10-Q
FDXF stake (3.3bn at market) is marked without haircut; disposal method and FDXF price both uncertain
Fiscal-year change (May -> December) breaks period comparability through 2027 and the Metrics CSV currently mislabels the last four quarters
